subject: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up and next steps

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a few follow-ups so we can size Dedicated for FintechX:

Key deployment preference you mentioned: dedicated capacity initially, with a long-term interest in Private VPC for compliance. For now we should size for Dedicated (reserved GPUs) and confirm VPC/networking needs if you proceed to Private later.

Questions / items I captured (please correct if I misremember):
- Approx target sustained TPS: 50 TPS (API calls/sec) with peaks up to ~200 TPS during end-of-day batch processing windows.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent requests ~25, peak concurrency ~60.
- Token mix: median prompt ~200 tokens, median completion ~800 tokens; occasional long-context sessions up to 4k tokens.
- Models: mix of 13B (inference-efficient) for most routing and a few heavy 70B instances for highest-quality generation.
- Latency SLO: 95p latency target ~500-800ms for 13B; ~1.5-2s acceptable for 70B in some workflows.
- Data residency: US-only; possibility of expanding to EU later.

Preliminary sizing questions for your side:
1) Can you confirm the ratio of 13B vs 70B traffic (est %)?
2) Are there predictable daily/hourly peaks (times) beyond the single end-of-day spike?
3) Any plans for streaming responses (token-by-token) vs. full-response generation only?

Attached is our dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx — if you can drop the numbers in the shaded cells we can produce a more concrete GPU estimate.

Suggested next steps:
- You fill the sheet and return (or we can walk through it together).
- 30-45 minute sizing workshop with Rafael (inference lead) and Aditya (solutions infra) — can do next week.
- I'll include a preliminary cost/throughput matrix for A100 vs H100 options once we get the completed sheet.

Would Tuesday or Wednesday next week work for a quick workshop?

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx (spreadsheet - sizing inputs)

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up and next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks great. A few quick answers and clarifications before we fill the sheet:

- 13B vs 70B split: we expect ~85% of traffic to be served by 13B models, 15% to hit 70B (quality-critical flows).
- Peaks: primary peak is at 6pm PST (end-of-day batch/summary generation) and a secondary peak around 1pm PST. Peaks typically last 15-30 minutes.
- Streaming: mostly full-response generation today; we may enable streaming for a subset of interactive sessions later.

Rough traffic numbers to help with the sheet:
- Sustained TPS: 50 requests/sec
- Peak TPS (15-30 min): 200 requests/sec
- Average token mix: prompt ~200 tokens, completion ~800 tokens (we do a lot of long summaries).
- Concurrent sessions (typical): ~25; peak concurrent: ~60.

Questions for you:
1) Is A100 OK or do you recommend H100 given the heavy long-context completions?
2) For the dedicated offering, what's the expected warmup time for model KV cache on burst traffic?

We can do the workbook walk-through Tue May 25 at 10am PT if that works for your team. I'll attach our security questionnaire — we'll need that for procurement.

Thanks,
Sophie
Head of Product
FintechX

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Chen <sophie.chen@fintechx.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing - follow-up and next steps

Thanks Sophie — helpful detail, and Tue 25th 10am PT works for us. Quick answers and a preliminary sizing note below. Rafael and Aditya, loop you in for the workshop.

A100 vs H100 guidance:
- For the 13B workload (85% of traffic): A100 (80GB) is generally cost-effective and will meet sub-second latency for median completions.
- For the 70B workload and long-context workloads (up to 4k tokens): H100 offers better throughput and lower p95 latency for the same model size due to NVLink and newer tensor cores — recommended if 70B traffic increases or tight latency is required.

Preliminary, high-level GPU estimates (very rough — will refine after sheet):
- Option A (A100-first): 13B traffic sized on 2-3x A100 GPUs (for 50 sustained TPS) + 3-4x A100 for peak headroom (or shared burst pool). For 70B traffic we would place 2-3x A100s (batch/low-priority) — but may see higher latency.
- Option B (H100-mix): 4x H100 to comfortably cover sustained 50 TPS across mixed 13B/70B with 2x H100 available for peak surges (total 6x). This gives better p95 latency for 70B and long completions.

Cache/warmup behavior:
- KV cache warmup for a cold model is per-session; typical warmup latency is small for small prompt sizes, but for long-context sessions it can add ~100-300ms for first few tokens while we populate key/value caches. Our Dedicated product supports pre-warmed model pools and prefix caching for predictable workloads (we can discuss pre-warm strategies in the workshop).

Next steps:
- We'll draft a short sizing summary after you return the sheet.
- Rafael and Aditya will bring a recommended baseline config (GPU counts, memory, network) to the Tuesday workshop.
- I'll also include a cost comparison A100 vs H100 in the prep doc.

See you Tue 25th 10am PT — calendar invite coming.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
